decisions.title: Ship Dr. Markdown as a local Wails desktop app
decisions.context: The application is targeted at macOS and embeds frontend assets through Wails rather than serving a website.
decisions.decision: Use Wails to host the editor UI locally and bind native Go document operations into the frontend.
consequences: The frontend can remain static assets embedded in the binary
Native file dialogs and close guards live in Go
Browser-only behavior must be suppressed or replaced where it leaks into the desktop UX

decisions.title: Keep filesystem access behind the Wails Go API
decisions.context: The frontend shell runs in a webview and should not directly read or write local files.
decisions.decision: Route open, save, save-as, dirty-state, and unsaved-change guard behavior through Wails-bound Go methods.
consequences: E2E tests can stub bridge methods without native dialogs
Document IO stays testable as a Go package
The frontend owns editor state but not filesystem writes

decisions.title: Write saved documents atomically
decisions.context: Markdown saves should not leave a truncated target file if the process fails mid-write.
decisions.decision: Write content to a same-directory temp file, fsync, close, and rename over the target path.
consequences: Save behavior is covered by focused Go unit tests
Write failures remove the temp file when possible

decisions.title: Use vendored editor bundles
decisions.context: The frontend is currently static assets under frontend/dist and does not depend on an npm build at runtime.
decisions.decision: Use vendored Milkdown Crepe, Highlight.js, Mermaid, and editor bundles through small local adapters.
consequences: The app can build through Wails without npm install/build commands
Editor capabilities are limited to what the vendored bundles expose
Raw and Split source highlighting plus fenced-code highlighting are backed by the shared Highlight.js adapter
Mermaid assistant previews and Mermaid fenced-block rendering are backed by the shared Mermaid adapter
Raw hide-markers still require a future editable token/decoration layer

decisions.title: Do not render decorative enabled controls
decisions.context: The current screen is being brought to functional parity before moving through concept screens.
decisions.decision: Visible enabled controls must either mutate state, call a native bridge, or be removed until their subsystem exists.
consequences: Preview, Share, Export, Split, fake docs rows, and unsupported marker hiding are deferred rather than faked
E2E tests enforce that shell buttons are backed

decisions.title: Persist backed runtime settings natively
decisions.context: The Settings concept includes application preferences, Sync, Git, extensions, and markdown flavour choices. The implemented settings slice now has a native JSON preference store, but the broader Sync, Git, Extensions, and Markdown flavour subsystems remain unimplemented.
decisions.decision: Persist backed Editor and Appearance settings through the Wails Go API while keeping unbacked settings categories disabled.
consequences: Settings stage changes in the frontend and write the saved preference envelope through the native bridge
Theme, document font, document font size, system-derived code font, code ligatures, raw soft wrap, and raw line numbers survive app relaunch
Markdown flavour, Sync, Git, Extensions, Preview, Share, Export, and Help settings remain absent until their backing subsystems exist
